In [[mathematics]], a '''D-space''' is a [[topological space]] where for every [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighborhood]] assignment of that space, a [[Cover (topology)|cover]] can be created from the union of neighborhoods from the neighborhood assignment of some [[Closed set|closed]] [[Isolated point|discrete]] [[subset]] of the space.

== Definition ==
An open neighborhood assignment is a function that assigns an open neighborhood to each element in the set. More formally, given a topological space <math>X</math>. An open neighborhood assignment is a function <math>f: X \to N(X)</math> where <math>f(x)</math> is an open neighborhood.

A topological space <math>X</math> is a D-space if for every given neighborhood assignment <math>N_x : X \to N(X)</math>, there exists a closed discrete subset <math>D</math> of the [[space]] <math>X</math> such that <math>\bigcup_{x\in D}N_x=X</math>.

== History ==

The notion of D-spaces was introduced by Eric Karel van Douwen and E.A. Michael. It first appeared in a 1979 paper by van Douwen and Washek Frantisek Pfeffer in the [[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=van Douwen|first1=E.|last2=Pfeffer|first2=W.|year=1979|title=Some properties of the Sorgenfrey line and related spaces|url=http://msp.org/pjm/1979/81-2/pjm-v81-n2-p07-s.pdf|journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics|volume=81|issue=2|pages=371–377|doi=10.2140/pjm.1979.81.371|doi-access=free}}</ref> Whether every [[Lindelöf space|Lindelöf]] and [[Regular space|regular]] [[topological space]] is a D-space  is known as the '''D-space problem'''. This problem is among twenty of the most important problems of set theoretic topology.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Open problems in topology II|last=Elliott.|first=Pearl|date=2007-01-01|publisher=[[Elsevier]]|isbn=9780444522085|oclc=162136062}}</ref>

== Properties ==
* Every [[Menger space]] is a D-space.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Aurichi|first1=Leandro|title=D-Spaces, Topological Games, and Selection Principles|journal=Topology Proceedings|date=2010|volume=36|pages=107–122|url=http://topology.auburn.edu/tp/reprints/v36/tp36009.pdf|archive-date=2017-01-09|access-date=2017-01-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170109113902/http://topology.auburn.edu/tp/reprints/v36/tp36009.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* A subspace of a topological [[Linearly ordered set|linearly ordered]] space is a D-space [[iff]] it is a [[paracompact space]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=van Douwen|first1=Eric|last2=Lutzer|first2=David|date=1997-01-01|title=A note on paracompactness in generalized ordered spaces|url=https://www.ams.org/proc/1997-125-04/S0002-9939-97-03902-6/|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|volume=125|issue=4|pages=1237–1245|doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-97-03902-6|issn=0002-9939|doi-access=free}}</ref>
